sources.reason: Multi-architecture ROM inspection combines 68k, PowerPC and FCode knowledge. Inspected Capstone 68040 decoder and symbol handling; ROM architecture is not inferred solely from the host-machine name.

Portable DSP3210 toolchain for AV Macs and unreleased Amiga prototypes, not stock Amiga hardware. Explicit AI-assisted authorship; approximate and exact DAU backends differ. External Sail comparison is optional, not part of default tests.
Bank-aware analyzer and ZMA-style output with BIOS symbols. Mapper placement is heuristic, IX/IY coverage partial and runtime mapper writes not emulated; embedded data may be decoded as code.
Browser control-flow-following disassembler derived from dasm09. Source and tests present; code/data separation is a technique, not a guarantee every indirect target is recovered.
Preserved 1991 C disassembler. Source prominently records a long-branch handling bug; catalogue as historical tooling rather than an unqualified accurate decoder.

Human68k drive/buffer/stack inspection and XDF/HDF utilities. Sample has packed drive-state structures. Keep coherent root collection; individual tools have different native/host execution requirements.

Small diagnostic for resident 9SCDRV using _X_KPCHK.O. Upstream warns false detections and out-of-bounds reads can cause bus errors. UTF-8 source requires Shift-JIS conversion for native build; not run here.
Preserved 16-colour MAG overlay program using selected transparent colours and palettes. Delegates image decoding/display to external viewer; not a standalone MAG codec.
Delphi/VCL formatter and binary import/export for 68000 arrays. Explicit successor to 68kQuickData; do not count the replaced tool as another current implementation.

Console source expands multipart assembler input to an unsplit output. String-based include processing tailored to Mega Drive workflows; not a general assembler parser or proven semantic refactoring tool.

Europe ROM reconstruction with named 68000/Z80 source and editable asset pipelines. README specifies 870 assembly functions and one C function; 100% physical replacement is not complete semantic understanding. Own ROM required.

Agent-oriented workflow includes actual trace-to-symbolic-assembly generator and analysis scripts. All game-derived output generated locally; semantic progress distinguished from merely decoded bytes. Not a game decompilation itself.

Actual C gameplay for SMB and Lost Levels with external ROM assets. Missing Lost Levels ending audio and regression tests remain explicit. README denies AI-generated code/assets and directs contributions to Codeberg; that narrower claim is not proof no AI was used for anything.
Readable bank-switching assembly and IDA analysis. README calls it decompilation, but inspected deliverable is assembly; MMC3 conversion and further recovery remain TODO.
YAML sprites and TMX tiles become cc7800-specific C data, with MARIA layout keywords. Fat-pixel and sprite-height constraints explicit; output is not portable ordinary C for all compilers.

General cartridge/disassembly/graphics/audio and authoring tools used by separately tracked game analyses. Bank-layout exceptions and scope are explicit; upstream corpus coverage not independently reproduced.
FFT-driven audio-to-TIA register conversion with batari Basic/assembly outputs. Intended for simpler tones; short windows limit frequency precision and voices/complex songs are poor fits.
General PS1 emulator/debugger and development tooling derived from PCSX. Inspected debugger implementation; classify as reusable tooling, not a game-specific emulation port.

Qt tools for map/database/executable/asset inspection. KF2 is main target; other FromSoftware games largely have model/texture loading only. KF3 names may be wrong or objects absent; editing completeness not implied.
Defines MMIO, marks selected read-only references and applies CRC/length SDK signatures. Short functions intentionally skipped due to ambiguity; best-effort naming is not proof of unique identity.
Glyph-table extraction and menu patch/research tools with recorded runtime addresses and tile layouts. Focused text/font work, not a complete game decompilation or translation.

Actual protocol-server code and analysis scripts exist. Author explicitly says Claude Code wrote the project and warns documentation may be hallucinated; login progress is not verified full online restoration or complete decompilation.
Bank-aware interactive disassembly project with labels, graphics and analysis state. Early software warns saved work may be lost and exit does not auto-save; no stability guarantee.
Text patterns plus FLIRT/YARA/radare signatures for dated library revisions. Sample identifies BIOS-call wrappers. Signature matches are version-bound heuristics, not full source reconstruction.
Implemented Huffman/displacement/LZ-style decoder modes for custom game compression. Narrow data-format reconstruction, not entire game code.
Text-table and character-edit helpers with documented offset evidence. Broad EOF repointing and multiline rewriting remain experimental/unstable; no claim all ROM patches are safe or compatible.

8080/Z80/Z180/Z80N assembler with syntax conversion, tape outputs, optional SDCC and generated-code tests. Decoder/parser bodies reviewed; target-mode differences and external compiler requirements retained.

notes: Parent-only pass across 36 platform/type search lanes and 321 distinct results, plus a separately screened successor. Thirty-five additions, one explicit predecessor duplicate and three deferrals. Platform declarations and emitted formats override misleading repository names: CPC-named source still builds Spectrum snapshots. Tool output language distinguished from implementation language, including generated ASM in C-shaped wrappers and compiler-family names inherited in parser code. Original Tube ROM README corrects stale repository description. Build/fidelity claims remain attributed; no candidate code executed. AI disclosure recorded only where explicit, with narrow no-generated-code claim not expanded to categorical non-use. Preserve warnings about long branches, out-of-bounds diagnostic reads, copied debugger state, heuristic signatures, incomplete driver audio and speculative server documentation.
